sections.content: Use ya with the pretérito perfecto to say that an action has already happened. Ya normally appears between the auxiliary verb and the participle: He ya viajado is incorrect; Ya he viajado is the natural form. It can also appear at the end of a sentence for emphasis. This lesson focuses on completed actions that have happened before now.

items.english: I have already rented a bicycle.
We have already seen the landscape.

items.spanish: Carlos ya ha comprado un mapa.
items.english: Carlos has already bought a map.
They have already arrived at the river.

sections.content: The most useful pattern is ya + auxiliary + participle: Ya he visto, ya hemos llegado.
